simple.meaning: בְּאֻשִׁים (bᵉʼushîym) is a Hebrew word meaning “poison-berries.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: בְּאֻשִׁים (H891) appears 2 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Isaiah 5:2, with occurrences in Isaiah.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to בְּאֻשִׁים (H891) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in בְּאֻשִׁים (H891) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: בְּאֻשִׁים (bᵉʼushîym) / H891 is traced through Isaiah 5:2, Isaiah 5:4 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H891. beushim בְּאֻשִׁים noun [masculine] plural stinking or worthless things , wild grapes (Late Hebrew noun of individual meaning בְּאוּשָׁה ) (perhaps adjective omitted עֲנָבִים compare Di) Isa 5:2 , 4 of Yahweh's vineyard, Vulgae labruscae (see further De).
